proofs.proof_tex:
For \(j=0\), substitution of \(h_n=n^{-1/(2s)}\) into the assumed bias term gives \(h_n^s=n^{-1/2}\), while its stochastic term is
\[
 \sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n h_n^{D_0}}}
 =n^{-1/2+D_0/(4s)}\sqrt{\log n}
 =n^{-\beta}\sqrt{\log n}.
\]
Because \(D_0=d+1>0\), the stochastic order is no smaller than the bias order. The \(d\)-dimensional bound for \(p\) is faster and is therefore bounded by the same displayed order. For \(j=1\),
\[
 h_n^{s-1}=n^{-1/2+1/(2s)},
 \qquad
 \sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n h_n^{D_0+2}}}
 =n^{-1/2+(d+3)/(4s)}\sqrt{\log n}
 =n^{-\beta_1}\sqrt{\log n}.
\]
The stochastic exponent is the slower one because
\[
 \left(\frac12-\frac1{2s}\right)-\beta_1
 =\frac{d+1}{4s}>0.
\]
The restriction \(s>3(d+1)\) yields
\[
 \beta>\frac12-\frac1{12}=\frac5{12}
\]
and
\[
 \beta_1>
 \frac12-\frac{d+3}{12(d+1)}
 =\frac{5d+3}{12(d+1)}>0.
\]
Finally, unit-mass normalization of \(\widehat p\) and \(p\), followed by addition and subtraction of \(\int\partial_a m(a,w)\widehat p(w)\,dw\), gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \lvert\widehat\theta'(a)-\theta'(a)\rvert
 &\le \int\lvert\partial_a\widehat m(a,w)-\partial_a m(a,w)\rvert\widehat p(w)\,dw\\
 &\quad+\int\lvert\partial_a m(a,w)\rvert\lvert\widehat p(w)-p(w)\rvert\,dw\\
 &\le \lVert\partial_a\widehat m-\partial_a m\rVert_\infty
   +\lVert\partial_a m\rVert_\infty\lVert\widehat p-p\rVert_1.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The fixed-radius condition \(\texttt{ass:m-smooth}\) bounds \(\lVert\partial_a m\rVert_\infty\), the unit covariate cube gives \(\lVert\widehat p-p\rVert_1\le\lVert\widehat p-p\rVert_\infty\), and \(\beta_1<\beta\). Taking the supremum over \(a\in J\) proves the claimed conditional derivative order. Every probability order used above is an explicit premise of the narrowed statement; no rate is asserted for an unspecified sample map.

By the definition of \(\mathfrak B_n\) and the conditional zeroth-order rates,
\[
 \mathfrak B_n
 \le \max_k\lVert\widehat m_k-m\rVert_\infty
 \left(\max_k\lVert\widehat g_k-g\rVert_\infty+
       \max_k\lVert\widehat p_k-p\rVert_\infty\right)
 =O_P(n^{-2\beta}\log n).
\]
Consequently
\[
 n^{5/6}(\log n)^{3/2}\mathfrak B_n
 =O_P\!\left(n^{5/6-2\beta}(\log n)^{5/2}\right),
 \qquad
 \frac56-2\beta=-\frac16+\frac{d+1}{2s}<0,
\]
where the strict inequality follows from \(s>3(d+1)\). Polynomial decay dominates the logarithmic factor, proving the first conclusion.

Under \(\texttt{ass:p-bounds}\), \(\texttt{ass:overlap}\), and \(\texttt{ass:variance}\), every true denominator entering \(f\), \(e\), and \(\kappa\) is bounded away from zero, while the fixed Hölder radii and \(\texttt{ass:outcome-bound}\) bound the numerators. On a fixed neighborhood of this compact range, addition, multiplication, division, and the cube-root map away from zero are Lipschitz. Integration over the unit covariate cube is a contraction in supremum norm. Hence the conditional zeroth-order rates imply
\[
 \lVert\widehat\kappa-\kappa\rVert_{\infty,J}
 =O_P\!\left(n^{-\beta}\sqrt{\log n}\right).
\]
Dividing by the lower bound \(v_\kappa\) in \(\texttt{ass:variance}\) gives the asserted order for \(\mathfrak K_n\). Applying the same Lipschitz argument to
\[
 (f,q,r)\longmapsto\int_J\left\{\frac{f(a)q(a)^2}{4r(a)}\right\}^{1/3}da
\]
on the range fixed by overlap, strict slope, and variance gives
\[
 \lvert\widehat{\mathcal V}_n-\mathcal V(P)\rvert
 =O_P\!\left(n^{-\beta_1}\sqrt{\log n}+n^{-\beta}\sqrt{\log n}\right).
\]
Moreover, overlap, strict slope, and variance give directly
\[
 \mathcal V(P)\ge |J|\left(\frac{c_gc_\theta^2}{4V_\kappa}\right)^{1/3}>0.
\]
This uniform lower bound converts the absolute order to the displayed relative order.

For the fixed-kernel validation calculation, write \(\mu(a)=\int\phi(a,w)p(w)\,dw\) and
\[
 U_N=\frac1{N^2}\sum_{i,j=1}^N
 \mathbf 1\{A_i\in I\}\{\phi(A_i,W_j)-\mu(A_i)\}.
\]
The diagonal contribution is bounded by a constant times \(N^{-1}\). For the off-diagonal kernel, conditioning on its first observation gives zero. Its projection on the second observation is
\[
 q_I(w)=\mathbb E_P[\mathbf 1\{A\in I\}\{\phi(A,w)-\mu(A)\}],
\]
and the upper density bound gives \(\lVert q_I\rVert_\infty\le C h\). Thus the average of the second projections is \(O_P(h/\sqrt N)\) by independence in \(\texttt{ass:iid}\) and Chebyshev's inequality. The remaining degenerate kernel has second moment \(O(h)\), because its bounded square vanishes unless \(A\in I\); the variance formula for a degenerate order-two average, obtained by expanding the square and observing that only coincident index pairs survive conditional centering, gives order \(O(h/N^2)\), hence stochastic order \(O_P(\sqrt h/N)\). Since \(N\asymp n\), the three pieces prove the stated bound. At \(h=H_n=n^{-1/3}(\log n)^2\), multiplication by \(n^{2/3}\sqrt{\log n}\) gives respectively
\[
 n^{-1/6}(\log n)^{5/2},\qquad
 n^{-1/2}(\log n)^{3/2},\qquad
 n^{-1/3}(\log n)^{1/2},
\]
all tending to zero. This is a fixed-kernel calculation and therefore does not supply the missing fitted-kernel supremum.

For the deterministic optimization statement, put
\[
 L_X(v)=\int v^2\,dt-2\int v\,dX.
\]
If \(H=X-\widetilde X\), integration by parts, \(\lVert H\rVert_\infty\le\eta\), \(\lVert v\rVert_\infty\le M_0\), and \(\operatorname{TV}(v)\le2M_0\) imply
\[
 \lvert L_X(v)-L_{\widetilde X}(v)\rvert
 =2\left|\int v\,dH\right|
 \le 2\eta\{\operatorname{TV}(v)+2M_0\}
 \le8M_0\eta.
\]
Taking infima changes each of the constrained and unrestricted optimized values by at most \(8M_0\eta\); the triangle inequality gives \(16M_0\eta\) for their difference. The envelope and common localization are explicit premises here and are not consequences of the four scalar clauses defining \(\mathsf G_n\).

The cited fixed-location result \(\texttt{lem:banerjee-wellner-fixed-location-lr}\) gives that \(D(0)\) is finite and nonnegative almost surely. For fixed \(x\), define the two-sided increment process
\[
 \mathbb W_x(t)=\mathbb W(x+t)-\mathbb W(x),\qquad t\in\mathbb R.
\]
The definition of \(X\) gives the pathwise identity
\[
 X(x+t)-X(x)-2xt=\mathbb W_x(t)+t^2.
\]
Translation of the horizontal coordinate and subtraction of an affine function commute with taking greatest convex minorants: if \(G\) is a greatest convex minorant of a function \(F\), then \(t\mapsto G(x+t)-G(x)-2xt\) is the greatest convex minorant of \(t\mapsto F(x+t)-F(x)-2xt\). The same equivariance holds for each one-sided constrained minorant, and the slope constraint \(2x\) becomes the origin constraint \(0\). Substituting \(s=x+t\) in the energy integral therefore gives
\[
 D(x)=\Phi(\mathbb W_x),
\]
where \(\Phi\) is the origin-constrained energy from \(\texttt{def:excursion-regime}\). A two-sided standard Brownian motion has stationary Gaussian increments, so \(\mathbb W_x\stackrel d=\mathbb W\). Hence \(D(x)\stackrel d=D(0)\), proving finiteness and nonnegativity at each fixed \(x\). The intersection of these probability-one events over a finite deterministic collection still has probability one.

For joint stationarity, the centered Gaussian vector process
\[
 \bigl(\mathbb W_{x_1+r}(t),\ldots,\mathbb W_{x_m+r}(t):t\in\mathbb R\bigr)
\]
has the same covariance function as the corresponding process with \(r=0\), because all covariances are determined by increments and a common translation leaves increment lengths and overlaps unchanged. Its mean is zero, so the two vector processes have the same finite-dimensional law. Applying the same measurable fixed-location GCM-energy maps coordinatewise proves the displayed stationarity identity. The argument is deliberately finite-dimensional and supplies none of the omitted continuum regularity claims.

Write \(F_h(t)=t^2+h(t)\). The dilation satisfies
\[
 F_{h_b}(bt)=b^2F_h(t).
\]
If \(G_h\) is the unrestricted greatest convex minorant of \(F_h\), then \(t\mapsto b^2G_h(t/b)\) is convex, lies below \(F_{h_b}\), and dominates every other convex minorant after applying the inverse dilation. It is therefore the greatest convex minorant of \(F_{h_b}\). The same order-preserving argument applies separately to the left and right constrained minorants. Their slopes are multiplied by \(b\). Thus the change of variables \(t=bs\) in the squared-slope energy gives
\[
 \Phi(h_b)=\int_{\mathbb R}b^2\{\text{unscaled squared-slope difference at }s\}\,b\,ds
 =b^3\Phi(h).
\]
For an absolutely continuous \(h\), \(h_b'(t)=b h'(t/b)\) almost everywhere, and hence
\[
 \frac12\int_{\mathbb R}\{h_b'(t)\}^2dt
 =\frac12\int_{\mathbb R}b^2\{h'(t/b)\}^2dt
 =b^3\frac12\int_{\mathbb R}\{h'(s)\}^2ds.
\]

Take \(b=u^{1/3}\) and \(\varepsilon=u^{-1/2}=b^{-3/2}\). Brownian scaling follows directly from the zero mean and covariance of two-sided Brownian motion and gives
\[
 b^{1/2}\mathbb W(\,cdot\,/b)\stackrel d=\mathbb W.
\]
But \((\varepsilon\mathbb W)_b(t)=b^2\varepsilon\mathbb W(t/b)=b^{1/2}\mathbb W(t/b)\). The first homogeneity and fixed-location well-posedness therefore yield
\[
 D(0)=\Phi(\mathbb W)stackrel d=\Phi((\varepsilon\mathbb W)_b)
 =b^3\Phi(\varepsilon\mathbb W)=u\Phi(u^{-1/2}\mathbb W),
\]
which proves the probability identity.

For the action lower bound, let \(y(t)=2t+h'(t)\). In the affine Hilbert space \(2t+L^2(\mathbb R)\), let \(\mathcal C\) be the closed convex set of nondecreasing slopes and let \(\mathcal C_0\subset\mathcal C\) be the closed convex set obeying the origin split constraint. The baseline \(r_0(t)=2t\) belongs to \(\mathcal C_0\). The GCM slope is the corresponding least-squares projection. Indeed, on any finite interval, if \(G\) is the GCM of a primitive of \(y\), \(g=G'\), and \(H=\int y-G\), then \(H\ge0\), the measure \(dg\) is supported on \(\{H=0\}\), and integration by parts gives the projection variational inequality
\[
 \int(y-g)(v-g)=-\int H\,d(v-g)\le0
 \qquad(v\in\mathcal C).
\]
The left and right capped/floored calculation gives the same inequality for \(\mathcal C_0\); exhaustion of \(\mathbb R\) gives the affine-space identity used below. Therefore
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 0\le\Phi(h)
 &=\operatorname{dist}^2(y,\mathcal C_0)-\operatorname{dist}^2(y,\mathcal C)\\
 &\le\operatorname{dist}^2(y,\mathcal C_0)
 \le\lVert y-r_0\rVert_2^2
 =\lVert h'\rVert_2^2.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Thus \(\Phi(h)\ge1\) implies \(\frac12\lVert h'\rVert_2^2\ge1/2\), and taking the infimum proves \(I_\star\ge1/2\).

For the explicit upper witness, put \(k=4^{1/3}\), \(a=k/4\), and
\[
 h'(t)=(k-2t)\mathbf 1\{-a\le t\le k/2\}.
\]
Then
\[
 y(t)=2t+h'(t)=
 \begin{cases}
 2t,&t<-a,\\
 k,&-a\le t\le k/2,\\
 2t,&t>k/2,
 \end{cases}
\]
which is nondecreasing because \(-2a=-k/2<k\) and \(2(k/2)=k\). Hence its unrestricted projection is itself. The origin-constrained projection agrees with \(y\) outside \([-a,0]\) and equals zero on \([-a,0]\). Call this candidate \(z\). It is nondecreasing and satisfies the split constraint. For every other constrained slope \(v\), one has \(v(t)\le0=z(t)\) for \(t\in[-a,0]\), while \(y-z=0\) off this interval. Hence
\[
 \int_{\mathbb R}(y-z)(v-z)dt
 =k\int_{-a}^0v(t)dt\le0.
\]
This is the Hilbert projection variational inequality, so \(z\) is the constrained projection. Consequently
\[
 \Phi(h)=\int_{-a}^0 k^2dt=ak^2=\frac{k^3}{4}=1.
\]
Direct integration gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \frac12\lVert h'\rVert_2^2
 &=\frac12\int_{-a}^{k/2}(k-2t)^2dt
 =\frac{(k+2a)^3}{12}\\
 &=\frac{(3k/2)^3}{12}=\frac98,
 \end{aligned}
\]
because \(k^3=4\). This admissible witness proves \(I_\star\le9/8\). The argument is deterministic; without exponential tightness and a continuity theorem for the infinite-domain GCM map it gives no large-deviation principle, and even such a principle alone would not give a sharp Palm prefactor or an additive tail ratio.

By \(\texttt{ass:p-normalization}\) and \(\texttt{ass:overlap}\), for every \(a\in J\),
\[
 c_g=c_g\int p(w)dw
 \le f(a)=\int g(a\mid w)p(w)dw
 \le C_g\int p(w)dw=C_g.
\]
The strict-slope and variance assumptions give
\[
 c_\theta\le\theta'(a)\le C_\theta,
 \qquad
 v_\kappa\le\kappa(a)\le V_\kappa.
\]
All factors in the definition of \(h_n(a)\) are therefore positive. Monotonicity of multiplication, division by positive numbers, and the cube root yields
\[
 \left(\frac{4v_\kappa}{nC_gC_\theta^2}\right)^{1/3}
 \le h_n(a)\le
 \left(\frac{4V_\kappa}{nc_gc_\theta^2}\right)^{1/3},
\]
which is the claimed uniform display after multiplication by \(n^{1/3}\). Inverting the positive definition gives the exact pointwise identity
\[
 h_n(a)^{-1}=n^{1/3}
 \left\{\frac{f(a)\theta'(a)^2}{4\kappa(a)}\right\}^{1/3}.
\]
The preceding two-sided bounds put the derivative of \(\Psi_{n,P}\) between two positive finite multiples of \(n^{1/3}\); hence \(\Psi_{n,P}\) is strictly increasing and bi-Lipschitz on the compact interval \(J\). Integrating the pointwise identity over \(J\) and invoking \(\texttt{def:spatial-clock}\) proves that its image length is exactly \(T_n(P)\). No probabilistic approximation has been used.

The bounds \(c_g\le f(a)\le C_g\), proved in \(\texttt{thm:causal-transfer}\), together with \(\texttt{ass:strict-slope}\) and \(\texttt{ass:variance}\), imply pointwise on \(J\)
\[
 \left(\frac{c_gc_\theta^2}{4V_\kappa}\right)^{1/3}
 \le
 \left\{\frac{f(a)\theta'(a)^2}{4\kappa(a)}\right\}^{1/3}
 \le
 \left(\frac{C_gC_\theta^2}{4v_\kappa}\right)^{1/3}.
\]
Integration over \(J\) proves the volume bounds. Since \(\delta\in(0,1/2)\), \(|J|=1-2\delta>0\); thus the lower constant is positive. Multiplication by \(n^{1/3}\) proves \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}T_n(P)\to\infty\).

Now suppose the two explicit conditional premises in the second part hold. Relative clock consistency and \(\widehat T_n/T_n(P)=\widehat{\mathcal V}_n/\mathcal V(P)\) give
\[
 \log\frac{\widehat T_n}{T_n(P)}=o_P(1)
\]
uniformly. The deterministic lower bound just proved makes \(T_n(P)\to\infty\) uniformly; relative consistency then also makes \(\widehat T_n\to\infty\) uniformly in probability. Hence both inverse centerings eventually lie in the increasing domain and diverge. By the mean-value theorem, for a point \(\widetilde b_n\) between the two inverse centerings,
\[
 \mathcal E'(\widetilde b_n)
 \{b_{\mathcal E}(\widehat T_n)-b_{\mathcal E}(T_n(P))\}
 =\log\frac{\widehat T_n}{T_n(P)}.
\]
Since \(\mathcal E'(u)=\beta+\gamma/u\to\beta>0\),
\[
 \frac{b_{\mathcal E}(\widehat T_n)-b_{\mathcal E}(T_n(P))}{a_{\mathcal E}(T_n(P))}
 =\frac{\mathcal E'(b_{\mathcal E}(T_n(P)))}{\mathcal E'(\widetilde b_n)}
 \log\frac{\widehat T_n}{T_n(P)}
 =o_P(1).
\]
The same derivative limit gives
\[
 \frac{a_{\mathcal E}(\widehat T_n)}{a_{\mathcal E}(T_n(P))}
 =\frac{\mathcal E'(b_{\mathcal E}(T_n(P)))}{\mathcal E'(b_{\mathcal E}(\widehat T_n))}
 \to1.
\]
These are implications of the stipulated future excursion form and clock consistency; neither premise is proved by this calculus.

Fix \(k\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and define
\[
 L_k(t)=\min_{v\in\mathcal C_n,\,v_k=t}
 \sum_{i=1}^n(Z_{(i)}-v_i)^2.
\]
The feasible set is nonempty because it contains the constant vector \(t\mathbf 1\); it is closed, and the coercive squared loss attains its minimum. If \(v^{(1)}\) and \(v^{(2)}\) are feasible at \(t_1\) and \(t_2\), then for \(\lambda\in[0,1]\), convexity of \(\mathcal C_n\) gives
\[
 \lambda v^{(1)}+(1-\lambda)v^{(2)}\in\mathcal C_n,
 \qquad
 [\lambda v^{(1)}+(1-\lambda)v^{(2)}]_k
 =\lambda t_1+(1-\lambda)t_2.
\]
Convexity of squared loss and minimization therefore show
\[
 L_k(\lambda t_1+(1-\lambda)t_2)
 \le\lambda L_k(t_1)+(1-\lambda)L_k(t_2).
\]
Thus \(L_k\) is finite and convex on \(\mathbb R\), hence continuous. Subtracting the unrestricted minimum does not change convexity, so
\[
 Q_n(a,t)=L_{k(a)}(t)-min_{v\in\mathcal C_n}\sum_{i=1}^n(Z_{(i)}-v_i)^2
\]
is continuous and convex in \(t\). Its finite sublevel sets are therefore closed intervals; when the threshold is \(+\infty\), the sublevel set is \(\mathbb R\). Because \(\widehat\kappa(a)>0\), direct substitution of the definitions gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \{\theta(a)\in\mathcal C_n(a)\ \forall a\in J\}
 &=\left\{Q_n(a,\theta(a))/\widehat\kappa(a)
       \le\widehat q_{n,\alpha}\ \forall a\in J\right\}\\
 &=\left\{\sup_{a\in J}Q_n(a,\theta(a))/\widehat\kappa(a)
       \le\widehat q_{n,\alpha}\right\}\\
 &=\{S_n(\theta)\le\widehat q_{n,\alpha}\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
On this event, \(\theta\) is a nondecreasing selector of the profile sets by \(\texttt{ass:monotone}\). Applying the deterministic image map in \(\texttt{def:crossing-set}\) to this particular selector produces exactly \(\tau_\zeta\), with the same empty-set and left-endpoint conventions. Hence the image contains the true observed-law crossing whenever the common LR event occurs. No step evaluates the probability of that event.

Substitution of the three constant functions into \(\texttt{def:spatial-clock}\) gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathcal V(P)
 &=\int_J\left(\frac{f_0r_0^2}{4\kappa_0}\right)^{1/3}da
 =|J|\left(\frac{f_0r_0^2}{4\kappa_0}\right)^{1/3},\\
 T_n(P)
 &=n^{1/3}\mathcal V(P)
 =n^{1/3}|J|\left(\frac{f_0r_0^2}{4\kappa_0}\right)^{1/3}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The inverse local scale from \(\texttt{thm:causal-transfer}\) is then the constant
\[
 h_n(a)^{-1}=n^{1/3}\left(\frac{f_0r_0^2}{4\kappa_0}\right)^{1/3},
\]
so its integral from \(\inf J\) to \(a\) is affine and its total image length is the displayed \(T_n(P)\). For one fixed canonical constraint point \(x\), the identity
\[
 X(x+t)-X(x)-2xt=\mathbb W_x(t)+t^2
\]
from \(\texttt{lem:canonical-wellposedness}\) translates the constraint to zero and subtracts its tangent. Affine equivariance of both GCM problems then gives \(D(x)=\Phi(\mathbb W_x)\stackrel d=D(0)\). This proves only the fixed-location identity and the constant-clock algebra.

added_lemmas.statement: For the fixed origin constraint, the Brownian--GCM likelihood-ratio functional \(D(0)\) in \(\texttt{def:canonical-field}\) is a finite nonnegative random variable almost surely.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Let \(D_0=d+1\). Consider any fully specified measurable boundary local-polynomial implementation represented by \(\widehat\eta\) for which, for \(j\in\{0,1\}\) and every \(D_0\)-dimensional primitive \(h\in\{g,m,r\}\),
\[
 \max_{1\le k\le K}\lVert\partial_a^j\widehat h_k-\partial_a^j h\rVert_\infty
 =O_P\!\left(h_n^{s-j}+\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n h_n^{D_0+2j}}}\right),
\]
with the analogous, no-slower, bound of dimension \(d\) for \(p\). At the frozen bandwidth \(h_n=n^{-1/(2s)}\), this premise implies
\[
 \max_k\lVert\widehat h_k-h\rVert_\infty
 =O_P\!\left(n^{-\beta}\sqrt{\log n}\right),
 \qquad \beta=\frac12-\frac{d+1}{4s}>\frac5{12},
\]
for \(h\in\{p,g,m,r\}\), and
\[
 \lVert\widehat\theta'-\theta'\rVert_{\infty,J}
 =O_P\!\left(n^{-\beta_1}\sqrt{\log n}\right),
 \qquad \beta_1=\frac12-\frac{d+3}{4s}>0,
\]
provided the density normalization is measurable and produces a nonnegative unit-mass estimate. This is a conditional implementation-rate calculation, not a probability theorem for the underspecified family denoted by the frozen learner symbol.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The frozen learner denotes a family rather than one measurable sample map. The replacement retains exactly the verified bandwidth and exponent algebra for any fully specified implementation satisfying the displayed primitive bias--variance bounds.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Assume the conditional zeroth- and first-derivative rates in \(\texttt{lem:learner-rates}\) hold for a chosen measurable implementation. Then
\[
 \mathfrak B_n=O_P(n^{-2\beta}\log n),
 \qquad
 n^{5/6}(\log n)^{3/2}\mathfrak B_n=o_P(1).
\]
For denominator-safe plug-in maps on the fixed model bounds,
\[
 \mathfrak K_n=O_P\!\left(n^{-\beta}\sqrt{\log n}\right),
 \qquad
 \left|\frac{\widehat{\mathcal V}_n}{\mathcal V(P)}-1\right|
 =O_P\!\left(n^{-\beta_1}\sqrt{\log n}+n^{-\beta}\sqrt{\log n}\right).
\]
For one fold of size \(N\asymp n\), a fixed dose interval \(I\) of length \(h\), and a fixed bounded continuously differentiable kernel \(\phi\), the centered off-diagonal validation-fold statistic has order
\[
 O_P\!\left(\frac{h}{\sqrt n}+\frac{\sqrt h}{n}+\frac1n\right).
\]
Moreover, on a fixed compact interval, if both monotone optimization classes have envelope \(M_0\) and two primitives differ in supremum norm by at most \(\eta\), then their constrained-minus-unconstrained optimized LR values differ by at most \(16M_0\eta\). These conclusions neither establish \(\mathsf G_n\) for the fitted validation-fold process nor imply \(S_n-S_n^\circ=o_P(1)\) without common contact localization and a slope envelope.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The scalar remainder clauses do not supply a fitted-kernel maximal inequality, common contact localization, or a slope envelope. The replacement keeps the proved product, plug-in, fixed-kernel V-statistic, and deterministic optimized-value calculations and expressly withholds optimized LR transfer.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For every finite deterministic collection \(x_1,\ldots,x_m\in\mathbb R\), the variables \(D(x_1),\ldots,D(x_m)\) are finite and nonnegative almost surely. Moreover, for every \(r\in\mathbb R\),
\[
 (D(x_1+r),\ldots,D(x_m+r))\stackrel{d}{=}(D(x_1),\ldots,D(x_m)).
\]
No separable locally bounded version, continuum contact-radius bound, or block-independence conclusion is asserted.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: Banerjee and Wellner support fixed-location well-definedness only. Brownian translation proves finite-dimensional stationarity, but no argument establishes separability, local boundedness, a continuum contact-radius tail, or block independence.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Let \(\Phi(h)\) be the origin-constrained deterministic Brownian--GCM likelihood-ratio energy generated by \(t^2+h(t)\), and, for \(b>0\), let \(h_b(t)=b^2h(t/b)\). Whenever these energies are defined,
\[
 \Phi(h_b)=b^3\Phi(h).
\]
If \(h\) is absolutely continuous, \(h(0)=0\), and \(h'\in L^2(\mathbb R)\), then
\[
 \frac12\lVert h_b'\rVert_2^2=b^3\frac12\lVert h'\rVert_2^2.
\]
Consequently, for every \(u>0\),
\[
 \Pr\{D(0)>u\}=\Pr\{\Phi(u^{-1/2}\mathbb W)>1\}.
\]
For
\[
 I_\star=\inf\left\{\frac12\lVert h'\rVert_2^2:h(0)=0,\ h'\in L^2(\mathbb R),\ \Phi(h)\ge1\right\},
\]
one has the deterministic bracket
\[
 \frac12\le I_\star\le\frac98.
\]
The upper bound is attained as a witness value by \(k=4^{1/3}\), \(a=k/4\), and \(h'(t)=(k-2t)\mathbf 1\{-a\le t\le k/2\}\), for which \(\Phi(h)=1\) and \(\frac12\lVert h'\rVert_2^2=9/8\). No large-deviation limit or probability-tail rate is inferred from \(I_\star\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: Exact Brownian scaling and the deterministic action bracket are proved, whereas no infinite-domain large-deviation principle, sharp Palm expansion, additive ratio, anticlustering, Poisson/Gumbel law, or grid approximation is available. The replacement states only the proved scaling/action result.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:

 \frac12\lVert h_b'\rVert_2^2=b^3\frac12\lVert h'\rVert_2^2,
 \qquad
 \Pr\{D(0)>u\}=\Pr\{\Phi(u^{-1/2}\mathbb W)>1\},
\]
together with

\]
The upper endpoint is supplied by the compactly supported plateau witness \(h'(t)=(k-2t)\mathbf 1\{-k/4\le t\le k/2\}\), \(k=4^{1/3}\), which has \(\Phi(h)=1\) and action \(9/8\). This identifies the only scaling compatible with a Cameron--Martin analysis but proves neither an infinite-domain large-deviation principle nor any sharp probability asymptotic.

open_obligations.partial_result:
Let \(\Phi(h)\) be the deterministic likelihood-ratio energy at the origin obtained from \(\texttt{def:canonical-field}\) after replacing \(\mathbb W\) by an absolutely continuous function \(h\) such that \(h(0)=0\) and \(h'\in L^2(\mathbb R)\).  For \(b>0\), define
\[
 h_b(t)=b^2h(t/b).
\]
Horizontal dilation by \(b\) and vertical dilation by \(b^2\) commute with taking greatest convex minorants.  The corresponding unrestricted and split-constrained slopes are therefore multiplied by \(b\).  Changing variables \(t=br\) in the likelihood-ratio energy and in the Cameron--Martin action gives, respectively,
\[
 \Phi(h_b)=b^3\Phi(h)
 \qquad\text{and}\qquad
 \frac12\int_{\mathbb R}\{h_b'(t)\}^2\,dt
 =\frac{b^3}{2}\int_{\mathbb R}\{h'(r)\}^2\,dr.
\]
Brownian scaling gives \(\mathbb W(t/b)\stackrel{d}=b^{-1/2}\mathbb W(t)\).  With \(b=u^{1/3}\), the process \(\{(u^{-1/2}\mathbb W)_b(t):t\in\mathbb R\}\) consequently has the same law as \(\{\mathbb W(t):t\in\mathbb R\}\).  The first homogeneity identity now yields the exact distributional reduction
\[
 \Pr\{D(0)>u\}
 =\Pr\{\Phi(u^{-1/2}\mathbb W)>1\}.
\]
Thus the exact scaling singles out \(u\) as the Cameron--Martin action speed, but does not by itself establish a large-deviation principle.

Define the associated deterministic variational value by
\[
 I_\star=
 \inf\left\{
   \frac12\int_{\mathbb R}\{h'(t)\}^2\,dt:
   h(0)=0,\ h'\in L^2(\mathbb R),\ \Phi(h)\ge1
 \right\}.
\]
It satisfies the computable bracket
\[
 \frac12\le I_\star\le\frac98.
\]
For the lower bound, first restrict to a finite interval containing the portion on which the constrained and unconstrained fits differ.  Put \(y(t)=2t+h'(t)\), let \(\mathcal C\) be the closed convex cone of nondecreasing slopes on that interval, and let \(\mathcal C_0\subset\mathcal C\) be the cone satisfying the split constraint at zero.  If \(G\) is the greatest convex minorant of a primitive of \(y\), \(g=G'\), and \(H\) is that primitive minus \(G\), then \(H\ge0\) and the measure \(dg\) is supported on \(\{H=0\}\).  Integration by parts therefore gives the projection variational inequality
\[
 \int (y-g)(v-g)
 =-\int H\,d(v-g)\le0,
 \qquad v\in\mathcal C.
\]
The same argument on the two half-intervals, followed by capping the left slope above by zero and flooring the right slope below by zero, identifies the split-constrained GCM slope with the projection onto \(\mathcal C_0\).  Since the baseline slope \(r_0(t)=2t\) belongs to \(\mathcal C_0\), nestedness of the two cones and the projection identity imply
\[
 0\le\Phi(h)
 =\operatorname{dist}^2(y,\mathcal C_0)
  -\operatorname{dist}^2(y,\mathcal C)
 \le \operatorname{dist}^2(y,\mathcal C_0)
 \le \lVert y-r_0\rVert_2^2
 =\lVert h'\rVert_2^2.
\]
Increasing the finite interval through the support of the fit difference preserves this inequality.  Hence \(\Phi(h)\ge1\) entails \(\frac12\lVert h'\rVert_2^2\ge1/2\), which proves \(I_\star\ge1/2\).

For the upper bound, let \(k=4^{1/3}\), let \(a=k/4\), and choose the absolutely continuous perturbation whose derivative is
\[
 h'(t)=(k-2t)\mathbf 1\{-a\le t\le k/2\}.
\]
Then \(y(t)=2t+h'(t)\) equals \(k\) on \([-a,k/2]\) and equals \(2t\) elsewhere.  It is nondecreasing, so it is its own unrestricted fit.  The split-constrained fit differs only on \([-a,0]\), where the left-hand cap replaces \(k\) by zero.  Therefore
\[
 \Phi(h)=ak^2=\frac{k^3}{4}=1.
\]
Its action is
\[
 \frac12\int_{\mathbb R}\{h'(t)\}^2\,dt
 =\frac12\int_{-a}^{k/2}(k-2t)^2\,dt
 =\frac{(k+2a)^3}{12}
 =\frac98,
\]
proving \(I_\star\le9/8\) and giving an explicit finite-energy plateau witness.

These identities neither identify \(I_\star\) with a probability-tail rate nor determine \(\beta_\star\), \(\gamma_\star\), or \(c_\star\).  Indeed, even a hypothetical logarithmic equivalent
\[
 -\log\lambda(u)=\beta u+o(u)
\]
would not imply the required additive ratio: an \(o(u)\) remainder need not satisfy \(r(u+x)-r(u)\to0\) for fixed \(x\).  The additive ratio and prefactor require a sharp infinite-domain Palm Laplace expansion with a classified action minimizer modulo translation, transverse fluctuation control, and a multiplicity law.  Distant-block separation after contact truncation also does not establish short-range anticlustering within a rare contact configuration.  Thus the exact scaling, variational bracket, and plateau witness are the strongest proved conclusions; finite positive runs intensity, the uniform block law, additive tail ratios, and the Poisson/Gumbel limit remain open.
